verdict: All 34 references are cited at least once and every cited number [1]–[34] exists in the list, but every citation in the report occurs in Chapters 1 and 2 only: Chapters 3 to 9 (gap, objectives, architecture, proposed solution, progress, publications, plan) contain no citations at all, which an examiner will notice, so the ten 'cite' items above (Chapter 3 gap statement, DID/VC semantics in 3.3.2, 5.2 and 6.2, dynamic consent in 3.3.5 and 6.5, threshold precedent in 6.3) are the priority. Within Chapter 1 the citations are broadly appropriate but several groups attach studies to claims they do not cover (the guardian/institutional-authority scenario cited to [21, 9] instead of [31], DIDs/VCs cited to blockchain surveys [2, 7, 3], the UCON proposal [11] cited as evidence of traditional static access control, and multi-party approval cited to [20, 15]). The bibliographic entries are complete (authors, title, venue, volume/issue/pages, year) and the venues and years agree with S_full; remaining issues are minor style inconsistencies (subtitle capitalisation, the '(TMIS)' abbreviation in [27], the em dash in [22], the missing issue number in [20], uneven use of 'et al.' between [9] which lists ten authors and [12]/[31]/[33]/[34] which truncate, and [21] and [34] sitting out of alphabetical order, which should be left as is because renumbering two days before submission would risk breaking in-text citations).
